title: Memory Management
description: Understand how JavaScript allocates and frees memory, and the role of garbage collection.

quiz.question: Where are primitive values stored in JavaScript memory?
quiz.explanation: Primitive values (like numbers, booleans, null, etc.) are stored in the stack.

quiz.question: Where are objects and functions stored in JavaScript memory?
quiz.explanation: Objects and functions are stored in the heap because they can grow in size.

quiz.question: What is garbage collection in JavaScript?
quiz.explanation: JavaScript automatically removes objects that are no longer referenced to free up memory.

quiz.question: Which algorithm does JavaScript commonly use for garbage collection?
quiz.explanation: Modern JavaScript engines mostly use the mark-and-sweep algorithm for garbage collection.

quiz.question: What causes a memory leak in JavaScript?
options: Objects that are no longer needed but still referenced
quiz.correctAnswer: Objects that are no longer needed but still referenced
quiz.explanation: Memory leaks happen when unused objects are still kept in memory due to lingering references.

quiz.question: Which of the following best helps avoid memory leaks?
options: Removing event listeners when no longer needed
quiz.correctAnswer: Removing event listeners when no longer needed
quiz.explanation: Event listeners can cause memory leaks if not removed after use.

quiz.question: What does 'reachable' mean in garbage collection?
options: Can be accessed through code logic
Referenced or accessible from the root object
quiz.correctAnswer: Referenced or accessible from the root object
quiz.explanation: A reachable object is one that can be accessed through a chain starting from a root.

quiz.question: Which memory type grows dynamically and stores objects?
quiz.explanation: The heap is a large area of memory used for storing objects and dynamic data.

quiz.question: Which of the following variables will be garbage collected?
options: An object referenced in a closure
quiz.explanation: Only objects with no references at all are eligible for garbage collection.

quiz.question: Why is it important to understand memory management in JavaScript?
options: To avoid memory leaks and optimize performance
quiz.correctAnswer: To avoid memory leaks and optimize performance
quiz.explanation: Understanding memory helps in writing efficient and optimized applications.
